subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu document attachments lose their durable local reference after inline truncation

question: Should durable inbound attachment provenance become a shared managed-media/session contract, or may Feishu append a plugin-local attachment record to the persisted message body?
rationale: The representation controls filesystem disclosure, media lifetime, cross-agent isolation, and whether other channels inherit the same durable-reference guarantee; source inspection cannot determine that security boundary without owner intent.

options.title: Shared managed reference
options.body: Add an opaque durable media reference to the shared inbound/session contract and migrate Feishu to it, avoiding raw host paths and channel-specific semantics.

options.title: Feishu-local record
options.body: Append a structured Feishu-only attachment record to the persisted body, accepting a narrower fix and future cross-channel contract divergence.

options.title: Defer to storage isolation
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19330, although per-agent storage alone would not preserve the message-to-file mapping required here.

recommendation.title: Shared managed reference
recommendation.body: Add an opaque durable media reference to the shared inbound/session contract and migrate Feishu to it, avoiding raw host paths and channel-specific semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly affects Feishu inbound assembly, and the plugin README identifies this person as its community owner; shared-core media owners should additionally review the final contract.
